name: Black-billed Barbet
rangeDescription: Eastern sudan to western ethiopia, northeastern democratic republic of the congo, uganda, western kenya, and northern tanzania
description: A medium-sized black barbet with a mostly red head. With a good look, pale edges to the wing feathers are visible.

name: Blue-fronted Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Montane forest of central and southeastern sulawesi
description: Male shows an entirely blue hood, an olive back, and rufous underparts, including the belly. Female lacks the blue hood.

name: Rotuma Myzomela
rangeDescription: Rotuma island (northwest of fiji)
description: A striking myzomela with beautifully contrasting plumage. Has a red chest and flanks and a bright crimson back and rump.

name: Yellow-throated Leafbird
rangeDescription: Southwestern philippines (balabac, busuanga, palawan, and calamian)
description: A medium-sized bird of lowland forest canopy and edge on Palawan and neighboring islands. Joins mixed-species flocks, often with bulbuls, foraging for fruits and seeds.

name: Burmese Myna
rangeDescription: Myanmar and southwestern china (southwestern yunnan)
description: Medium-sized starling of forest edge, agricultural fields, and open scrubby or grassy areas. Thin, black bandit’s mask, medium-gray back, grayish-pink chest, dark iris and bicolored orange-and-black bill.

name: Biak White-eye
rangeDescription: Mountains of supiori and biak (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: A small bird of forest on Biak Island where it is the only white-eye. Olive-green head and back, yellow under the base of the tail, dark gray face, pale gray underparts with whitish throat and belly.

name: Piping Crow
rangeDescription: Central and southern sulawesi, muna, and buton islands
description: A distinctive black-and-white crow that occurs within the canopy of hill and mountain forest on Sulawesi and satellite islands. White parts of adults are duller on juveniles.

name: White-tailed Swallow
rangeDescription: Arid highlands of southern ethiopia (sidamo province)
description: A small swallow with white underparts and dark blue upperparts. The tail shows an unusual pattern: a dark rim around large white panels both above and below.

name: Tacarcuna Wood-Quail
rangeDescription: Far eastern panama and adjacent northwestern colombia (chocó)
description: This rare chickenlike bird has an exceptionally small range on the border between Panama and Colombia. Found on the ground in mature forest from around 1,000–1,400 m.

name: Yellow-bibbed Lory
rangeDescription: Eastern solomon islands
description: A thick-set, short-tailed parrot with green wings, a red body, a black cap, purple thighs, and a yellow bib just underneath a black streak on the side of the neck that extends up toward the cap. Resident in primary forest, but tolerant of modified habitats.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Heard Island Shag
rangeDescription: Heard island (southern indian ocean)
description: A large pied shag with a very white head, neck, and shoulders, a bright blue eye-ring, and a large patch of yellow warty skin in front of the eyes. Breeding adult has a wispy crest.

name: Thrush Nightingale
rangeDescription: Northern eurasia; winters to eastern and southern africa
description: Very similar to Common Nightingale, but more dusky brown (not reddish-brown), with a duller and darker rufous tail and a mottled brown (not plain and sandy) breast. Their songs can be confusingly similar, but Thrush Nightingale is more monotonous, less varied, and slower, resembling that of Song Thrush.

name: Cuban Emerald
rangeDescription: Cuba including isla de la juventud (isle of pines; south of western cuba), grand bahama, great abaco, and andros
description: A pugnacious hummingbird that feeds on flowers and insects and is sometimes found flycatching. Inhabits a broad range of habitats.

name: Western Dwarf Hornbill
rangeDescription: Sierra leone to northern democratic republic of the congo (west of the congo river)
description: A small, dark forest hornbill found predominantly in primary forest subcanopy, where it prefers areas with abundant vines. This species is unique in its overall dark coloration and its broad white eyebrow that extends to the back of the head.

name: White-necked Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Myanmar to southwestern china (southwestern yunnan), western thailand, and northwestern laos
description: Brown with a russet crown, black face and throat, and a small white patch on the upper neck. Looks like a darker-headed version of the similar Gray Laughingthrush.

name: Rusty-flanked Treecreeper
rangeDescription: Mountains of western nepal to northeastern myanmar, southeastern tibet, and southwestern china
description: Well-marked treecreeper with a tiny bill, warm brown upperparts, and a dark brown ear patch on a white face. Warm rusty tones on the sides contrast sharply with a clean white throat and may meld into dark upperparts at a distance.

name: Streak-capped Spinetail
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Mostly brown arboreal spinetail with a black-streaked rufous crown and rufous wings and tail. Has a narrow white eyebrow, diffuse pale streaks on face, and slightly downcurved bill.

name: Greater Spotted Eagle
rangeDescription: Central eurasia and southern asia; winters to africa, china, and indochina
description: Adults are large and quite uniform dark brown eagles with very broad wings and short tails. Single white

name: Chestnut Wood-Quail
rangeDescription: Western and central andes of colombia
description: This chickenlike bird is bright rufous on the face and underparts and brown above. Female similar to male but rufous more restricted to the upper breast with contrasting gray belly.

name: Black-crested Warbler
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to northern venezuela, ecuador, and northern peru
description: Small yellow warbler found in the understory of Andean forest and scrub from around 2,500-3,500m. Olive above and brighter yellow below, with bright yellow eyebrow and black crown.

name: Gray Crow
rangeDescription: New guinea, including raja ampat islands (off western new guinea), yapen (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea), and d'entrecasteaux archipelago (off southeastern new guinea)
description: A large bird of lowland and foothill forest canopy, often near rivers. Somewhat variable plumage but has a long tail, bare, pink, facial skin and blue eyes.

name: Lilac-tailed Parrotlet
rangeDescription: Northern venezuela to trinidad and tobago and the guianas
description: Small parrot of rainforest regions. Generally uncommon; distinctive black-and green plumage and purple tail render it unmistakable on the rare occasions it is seen well.

name: Inambari Woodcreeper
rangeDescription: Western amazonia, south of the amazon: eastern peru southward to bolivia and eastward to brazil west of the rio madeira
description: Fairly small woodcreeper with a thin, slightly downcurved bill. Extensive streaking on the undersides but almost no streaking on the head or back; when viewed from the back, appears very plain.

name: Red-legged Seriema
rangeDescription: Central and eastern brazil to bolivia, paraguay, and central argentina
description: Unmistakable large terrestrial raptorial bird. Sandy-colored overall with very long red legs, a long tail, and tufty crest in front of the eyes.

name: Madagascar Pratincole
rangeDescription: Madagascar; winters coastal somalia to northern mozambique
description: Dark, long-winged, elegant bird that is halfway between a tern and a shorebird in shape. Nests along rocky rivers and coastlines, and sometimes sits in open fields.

name: Seram Oriole
rangeDescription: Seram (southern moluccas)
description: A dull, entirely olive-brown oriole with a pale collar and a conspicuous dark face. Singles or pairs can be found in forest and forest edge in the lowlands and foothills, being more abundant lower down.

name: Chestnut Antpitta
rangeDescription: East slope of the andes of northern peru (amazonas south of the río marañón, southward to huánuco, and north of the río huallaga)
description: Plain antpitta restricted to cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes in northern Peru. Mostly chestnut-brown; very similar to Graves’s Antpitta, but lacks a distinct eyering and has a different voice.

name: Blackish-headed Spinetail
rangeDescription: Arid tropical southwestern ecuador to far northwestern peru (tumbes)
description: An uncommon spinetail found in dry forest in western Ecuador and northwestern Peru; threatened by habitat loss. Plumage is gray with a darker face and throat, rusty wings, and a long, grayish tail.

name: White-winged Coot
rangeDescription: Far southeastern brazil to eastern bolivia and southward to tierra del fuego
description: Fairly common to uncommon coot, mainly in lowlands. Found on fresh to brackish ponds and lakes and wetlands with open water.

name: Tawny-bellied Seedeater
rangeDescription: Bolivia to paraguay, southern brazil and northern argentina
description: Small finchlike species with a short and stubby bill. Males are gray above and tawny below with a tawny rump.

name: Orange-breasted Sunbird
rangeDescription: Heathlands and protea shrubs of southwestern cape province (south africa)
description: The male is a stunning sunbird with a fiery-orange belly and an iridescent purple breast band and green head. The female and juvenile are dull olive with slightly paler underparts.

name: Brown-cheeked Hornbill
rangeDescription: Humid forest of sierra leone to ghana
description: Big, spectacular black-and-white hornbill. Males have a large cream-colored bill, and females a much smaller and darker one.

name: Vanuatu Streaked Fantail
rangeDescription: Vanuatu and banks group
description: Small, with a long, often fanned tail. Gray above with a brownish back, speckled white chest, and elegant white eyebrow and cheek stripe.

name: Vietnamese Crested Argus
rangeDescription: Mountains of central vietnam and eastern laos
description: A large brown pheasant of humid forests, shy and extremely difficult to see. Most sightings are at dancing grounds, where males have cleaned the leaf litter from a large patch of the forest floor.

name: Brown Nightjar
rangeDescription: Locally from liberia to northern gabon and central democratic republic of the congo
description: A mottled reddish-brown forest nightjar with two distinctive white spots on either side of the throat. Perches on branches in the canopy and subcanopy, from which it can be seen hawking insects.

name: Ahanta Spurfowl
rangeDescription: Discontinuous in lowlands of senegambia to southwestern nigeria
description: Medium-sized dull gray-brown francolin with an orange-red bill and legs. With a good view, white streaks are evident on the neck and underparts.

name: Blue-banded Pitta
rangeDescription: Primary submontane forest of northern half of borneo
description: Unique-looking pitta of hill and submontane forests. Note bright red underparts, dull tan-orange face, dull blue-green back, and glittering silver-blue “necklace” and secondaries (similarly-colored line trailing down from behind the eye can be visible if seen well).

name: Beaudouin's Snake-Eagle
rangeDescription: Southwestern mauritania southward to guinea, eastward to southwestern sudan and western south sudan, possibly to northern uganda
description: Chunky dark brown raptor with a white belly marked by thin bars. Immatures are brown when perched, and show rufous patches in the underwing in flight.

name: Puerto Rican Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Puerto rico including isla de culebra and isla de vieques (both just east of puerto rico), and virgin islands
description: An inconspicuous woodland species often first detected by voice. It has a slender build and is colored dull brown above and mostly grayish white below.

name: Plumbeous Warbler
rangeDescription: Guadeloupe including terre-de-haut and marie-galante (just to south of guadeloupe) and dominica (central lesser antilles)
description: A striking small bird that frequents montane forests, but sometimes ventures into dry scrub and mangroves. This species is readily distinguished by its overall gray plumage (tinged green above and yellow below on immature birds) with boldly contrasting white eyebrows and wingbars.

name: Blue-billed Duck
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed southwestern and southeastern australia, including tasmania
description: Small stiff-tailed diving duck with a relatively slender dished bill. Floats very low in the water, and unlikely to be seen on land.

name: Yellowish Imperial-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Bismarck archipelago including admiralty islands
description: Large pigeon, mostly yellowish-white with black wing feathers. Tip of the tail also black.

name: Abyssinian Longclaw
rangeDescription: High grassland of ethiopia
description: A large and relatively colorful member of the pipit family. Note the black necklace, orange throat, and partially yellow eye-stripe.

name: American Wigeon
rangeDescription: Breeds alaska to southern usa; winters through central america and the caribbean
description: Breeding males have obvious white blaze on forehead and broad green slash behind eye. Females are plainer brown with rusty sides.

name: Yellow-throated Leafbird
rangeDescription: Southwestern philippines (balabac, busuanga, palawan, and calamian)
description: A medium-sized bird of lowland forest canopy and edge on Palawan and neighboring islands. Joins mixed-species flocks, often with bulbuls, foraging for fruits and seeds.

name: Black-chinned Yuhina
rangeDescription: Northern india eastward to central and southeastern china, southward to western myanmar, northern and central laos, vietnam, and far eastern cambodia
description: A small yuhina of open forest environments. Black chin is not very noticeable, but the black crest is.

name: Serendib Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Lowland rainforest of southwest sri lanka
description: Very small rufescent owl, with yellow-orange eyes, and sparse, light speckles on the underparts. Although does not possess true ear tufts it can show “false” ones when alert.

name: Sumatran Drongo
rangeDescription: Humid lowlands of sumatra
description: Glossy large-billed drongo with glossy blue-sheened wings and tail. Also note bright red eyes, iridescent speckling around the throat and neck, and flared broad-tipped tail.

name: Bush Thick-knee
rangeDescription: Inland southern trans-fly (south-central new guinea) and australia (except south-central and tasmania)
description: Distinctive large shorebird with long legs, enormous yellow eye, heavily streaked underparts. During the day stands or sits under small trees/shrubs, often in small groups.

name: Sociable Weaver
rangeDescription: Namibia and botswana to northern south africa
description: A small, dumpy buff-and-brown weaver with a blue-gray bill, a dark bib, and scaly patterning on the back and flanks. Juveniles are duller, lacking the bib and scaling.

name: Pied Thrush
rangeDescription: Himalayas of northern india from nepal to assam; winters to sri lanka
description: Slender, ground-dwelling thrush. Male is breathtakingly decked out in black and white.

name: Ecuadorian Thrush
rangeDescription: Coastal western ecuador (esmeraldas) to far northwestern peru (tumbes)
description: A common thrush of clearings and forest edge in most of western Ecuador; also reaches far northwestern Peru. Adult’s tan plumage, yellow bill, and orange eyering are distinct in its range.

name: Agami Heron
rangeDescription: Tropical southern mexico to northern bolivia and western amazonian brazil
description: Reclusive, rarely seen heron of humid tropical lowlands. Found along quiet forest streams and locally in mangroves.

name: Slaty-backed Thrush
rangeDescription: Eastern lesser sundas (yamdena and larat)
description: An unmistakable black, white, and gray thrush. Gray upperparts and black head marked with bold white cheek patch and long white eyebrow.

name: Rennell Starling
rangeDescription: Rennell and bellona (southeastern solomon islands)
description: A medium-sized, uniformly black starling with a glossy purplish-bluish sheen and a short tail. Bill is relatively thick and stubby.

name: Andean Lapwing
rangeDescription: Andes of southwestern colombia to northwestern argentina and northern chile
description: Large, boldly patterned shorebird of high Andean bogs, wetlands, and lakeshores; also ranges into grassy pastures in the northern part of its range. Usually in pairs or loose flocks, feeding with typical stop-start action of plovers.

name: Amami Thrush
rangeDescription: Amami ōshima (northern ryukyu islands, southern japan)
description: Large thrush, pale brown above, white below, with scale-like black-tipped feathers throughout the plumage. Inhabits undisturbed broadleaf evergreen forests of low elevations.

name: Clapperton's Spurfowl
rangeDescription: Sub-saharan africa (mali to sudan and ethiopia)
description: A medium-sized, pale francolin with large patches of red bare skin around the eyes. Heavily marked with black and pale buff on the back, neck, and underparts.

name: Black Cuckooshrike
rangeDescription: Angola to kenya, tanzania, mozambique, and south africa
description: Small, slim cuckooshrike in which males and females are strikingly different. Males are almost completely black with an odd pale patch at the base of the bill; some have a yellow shoulder Females are gray on the back and pale below, with heavy markings throughout.

name: Snow Mountain Quail
rangeDescription: Alpine grassland of snow mountains (west-central new guinea)
description: A huge quail of alpine grasslands. Plump, yellow bill and legs, black bars and white streaks on the back.

name: Usambara Double-collared Sunbird
rangeDescription: Highlands of southeastern kenya (taita hills) and northeastern tanzania
description: A medium-sized sunbird. Males are colorful, green and red, and females drab olive-brownish.

name: Starred Wood-Quail
rangeDescription: Tropical forest of western amazon basin
description: Rotund brown bird of lowland rainforest understory. Reddish brown with small gray spots.

name: Red-capped Robin
rangeDescription: Interior of southern australia, to southern and western coasts
description: Small Australian robin. Male black above, with a black head and chin, vivid scarlet breast and forecrown.

name: Violaceous Coucal
rangeDescription: New ireland and new britain (eastern bismarck archipelago)
description: A large, long-tailed, thick-billed bird, entirely dark bluish-black, with pale skin around a red eye. Found in most habitats, most commonly in old-growth lowland forest.

name: Pygmy Lorikeet
rangeDescription: Mountains of new guinea (bird's head peninsula to owen stanley range)
description: A tiny, green lorikeet of foothill and montane forest and edge. Uniform green plumage, light streaking on the chest and slightly elongated pointy tail.

name: Bolivian Warbling Finch
rangeDescription: Andes of bolivia and adjacent northwestern argentina (jujuy)
description: Striking tanager of open woodland and scrub in high elevations of the east slope of the Andes in central and southern Bolivia and extreme NW Argentina; including agricultural lands, and open Polylepis woodland. From Black-and-chestnut Warbling-Finch by white throat and paler underparts in Bolivian.

name: Scaled Fruiteater
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia and western venezuela to western bolivia (la paz)
description: Chunky, short-tailed, flat-headed bird patterned in mossy green and black. Scaly above and below with broad green wingbar and black cap.

name: Talaud Rail
rangeDescription: Karekelong island (talaud archipelago)
description: An unmistakable, little-known hulking forest rail with a large yellow bill, an all-rufous head and neck, forest-green upperparts, and a blackish belly. Also note the striking pale blaze behind the eye.

name: Tatama Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of colombian andes (western antioquia southward to southwestern valle del cauca)
description: This typical “Scytalopus” tapaculo is found only in Colombia’s western Andes. Plumage is gray with a brown tinge to the rump and faint, rusty barring on the lower underparts.

name: Gray Catbird
rangeDescription: Southern british columbia to gulf states; winters to west indies and panama
description: Medium-sized songbird with a smooth gray body, black cap, and rusty-red undertail coverts. Sexes alike.

name: Lesser Seedcracker
rangeDescription: Eastern tanzania to southern malawi, eastern zimbabwe, and northern mozambique
description: A colorful, chunky waxbill with a large conical bill. Both sexes have a red hood and tail, but females have slightly less extensive red.

name: Glossy Ibis
rangeDescription: Locally in eastern north and southern south america, africa, eurasia, to australasia
description: Long, curved bill. Adults mostly dark with iridescent green and reddish tones.

name: Araguaia Spinetail
rangeDescription: Pantanal of western brazil (araguaia valley)
description: Typical spinetail with a long spiky tail, a grayish-brown head, bright cinnamon wings and tail, a white throat, and pale buffy underparts. Sexes similar.

name: Broad-billed Tody
rangeDescription: Arid scrub and woodland of hispaniola including gonâve island
description: A small, gemlike species of woodlands including coffee plantations and mangroves. The rather large head, long bill, and short tail create a profile shared only by the Narrow-billed Tody within its range.

name: Western Tragopan
rangeDescription: Himalayas of northern pakistan to northwestern india and adjacent southwestern tibet
description: A large, short-tailed pheasant. Male appears mostly dark with prominent white dots all over.

name: Highland Elaenia
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of southern ecuador to bolivia and northwestern argentina
description: Medium-sized flycatcher with a small head and long tail. Found in forests and second growth.

name: Imeri Warbling-Antbird
rangeDescription: East-central colombia to southern venezuela and far northwestern amazonian brazil
description: Small antbird. Males are streaked black above, with a yellow-tinged throat and rusty flanks.

name: Dusky Tetraka
rangeDescription: Rainforest of east-central madagascar
description: Extremely rare and enigmatic tetraka. Dark olive-green overall, with a pale yellowish throat and ring around the eye.

name: Rufous Casiornis
rangeDescription: Southeastern peru to eastern bolivia, paraguay, northern argentina, and amazonian and eastern brazil
description: A large mostly cinnamon flycatcher with a paler breast and belly. Note the black bill with a pinkish base.

name: Spur-winged Lapwing
rangeDescription: Senegambia to red sea, northeastern tanzania, and eastern mediterranean
description: This medium-large plover is often locally abundant, noisy, and easy to identify. Its plumage is a striking combination of black, white, and brown.

name: Brown Firefinch
rangeDescription: Angola to democratic republic of the congo, zambia, southern tanzania, northern namibia, and northern zimbabwe
description: This is the darkest and dullest firefinch, the only species without a red or pink rump. Both sexes have red in the bill.

name: Plum-headed Finch
rangeDescription: Eastern australia (burdekin river, queensland to about sydney, new south wales)
description: Small brown bird with finely barred front. Brown above, paler and finely barred, below, with with pale spots on the wing and rump, pale-tipped tail, and tiny plum-colored cap (male also has plum-colored chin).

name: Campina Thrush
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia eastward to southern venezuela and guyana, southward locally to central amazonian brazil, from the east bank of the río madeira to the east bank of the río tapajós
description: A drab thrush, uncommon in open habitats and woodlands in the lowlands. Nondescript grayish-brown with a pale whitish belly.

name: White-breasted Antbird
rangeDescription: Central amazonian brazil to western mato grosso
description: Striking antbird with a conspicuous white throat and breast. Males have a black cap, brown back, and gray belly, while females have a cinnamon cap and underparts scaled black-and-chestnut.

name: Minute Hermit
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southeastern brazil (bahia to rio de janeiro)
description: Tiny hummingbird with a curved bill and a yellow lower bill. Males have a dark green iridescent back, a dark brown throat with a pale belly and vent, and dark undertail feathers.

name: Speckled Warbler
rangeDescription: Central and eastern queensland through new south wales to eastern and central victoria
description: Small, distinctive, ground-dwelling bird. Upperparts gray, underparts cream white, with black streaking on back, underparts, and crown.

name: Golden-tailed Parrotlet
rangeDescription: Eastern brazil (pernambuco to são paulo)
description: Small parrot with a short, squared tail. The body is largely green with distinctive brown bases to the wings and an orangey face.

name: Bornean Frogmouth
rangeDescription: Montane forest of borneo
description: Small stout frogmouth with a face full of wispy whiskers. Males are dark brown overall; females are bright rufous.

name: Dusky-tailed Antbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil to southeastern paraguay and northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: Medium-sized antbird with a long olive-brown tail. Found in the dense understory of humid forest, woodlands, and forest edges.

name: Blue-bellied Parrot
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southeastern brazil (southern bahia to rio grande do sul)
description: Fairly large parrot with a long tail and a pale bill. Mostly green with a blue tail tip and bluish underwings.

name: Socotra Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Socotra (off eastern somalia)
description: A small, compact, pale gray owl with tiny ear tufts. Found on the island of Socotra, where it inhabits arid habitats with trees, including palms.

name: Helmet Vanga
rangeDescription: Dense forest of northeastern madagascar
description: Huge black vanga with a rufous back and an enormous blue bill. Rare and localized Madagascar endemic that is found in northeastern rainforest at low and middle elevations.

name: Plumbeous Black-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern peru (cusco) to western bolivia and northern argentina
description: Medium-sized flycatcher of Andean slopes; rare in southern Peru, more common in Bolivia and northern Argentina. Male is separated from White-winged Black-Tyrant by grayer, less glossy plumage and from Cinereous Tyrant by darker belly.

name: Nonggang Babbler
rangeDescription: Limestone hills of southwestern guangxi (southeastern china), and in adjacent extreme northeastern vietnam (eastern tonkin)
description: A medium-sized brown babbler with pale eyes and a lopsided white crescent bordering the back half of the cheek. Short-tailed and large-headed in profile.

name: Belted Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Central and eastern canada to northern south america including trinidad and tobago and west indies
description: Stocky and large-headed with a shaggy crest. Bill is long, straight, thick, and pointed.

name: Great Dusky Swift
rangeDescription: Central and southern brazil to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina
description: Large swift with uniform cold brown plumage with a pale face. Similar to Sooty Swift, but is larger and paler.

name: Orange-eyed Flatbill
rangeDescription: Tropical southern colombia and northeastern peru north of the amazon
description: Rare flycatcher found in seasonally flooded swamp forest in lowlands east of the Andes. Pale eye, wide bill, buffy throat and breast, gray crown, and lack of facial markings help separate it from similar species such as Gray-crowned Flycatcher.

name: Temminck's Stint
rangeDescription: Northern palearctic; winters to africa, indonesia, and philippines
description: Breeds on wet moorland mainly in Scandinavia and Russia; migrants occur in wide variety of wetland habitats across Africa and southern Asia. Found mainly as singles or small groups, locally in flocks.

name: Chapada Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Cerrado region of brazil and adjacent eastern bolivia
description: Medium-sized flycatcher with a gray head, olive back, and yellow belly. Note the white rump contrasting with the dark tail, which has a broad white terminal band.

name: Choco Vireo
rangeDescription: Local on the pacific slope of colombia (risaralda and nariño) and northwestern ecuador (esmeraldas and pichincha)
description: Rare vireo found only in lush Andean cloud forest in northwestern Ecuador and western Colombia. In contrast to the much more common Brown-capped Vireo, it has pale wingbars and may show an ochraceous wash on the throat and breast.

name: Orinoco Piculet
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia, adjacent southern venezuela (southern amazonas), and northwestern brazil
description: This scarce piculet is known only from a few locations in the humid lowlands of eastern Colombia, southern Venezuela, and northwestern Brazil. Its underparts are entirely barred, but upperparts are plain, lacking the barring shown by the otherwise very similar Lafresnaye’s Piculet.

name: Sumatran Green-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Montane forest of sumatra and western java
description: Relatively plain and unmarked green-pigeon with a long pointed tail. Males have a faint orange blush on the chest, though this can be hard to notice.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Elegant Imperial-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Small islands off moluccas to eastern lesser sundas
description: A large pigeon of small islands. Shows a conspicuous pale yellow eye, a pale gray head and underparts, a chestnut vent, and a green back, wings, and uppertail.

name: Baird's Sparrow
rangeDescription: Great plains of north america; winters to southwestern usa and northern mexico
description: One of North America's most sought-after sparrows due to its small breeding range and secretive habits. Breeds in extensive tall grasslands; winters in similar grassy habitats.

name: White-gorgeted Fantail
rangeDescription: Malaita (central solomon islands)
description: Slender, with a long, often fanned tail. Dark above, with a white throat and belly, as well as a boldly white-streaked black chest.

name: Pincoya Storm-Petrel
rangeDescription: Known only from waters near chiloé island (reloncavi sound and the chacao channel), chile
description: Very local in inshore marine waters near Puerto Montt, Chile, where it can be locally numerous. Similar to the common and widespread Wilson’s Storm-Petrel (and may simply be a localized population of that species), but averages more white in plumage, especially on underwing and vent area.

name: Chilean Swallow
rangeDescription: Breeds southern chile and argentina; winters north to bolivia and brazil
description: Common and familiar swallow of southern South America; found widely from the coast to Andean foothills and from open forests to beaches. Often near water and regularly around towns and villages, associating readily with slightly smaller Blue-and-white Swallow.

name: White-gaped Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Northern australia (king sound, western australia to townsville, queensland)
description: A medium to large honeyeater with a sooty brown plumage and a bright pale patch between its eye and bill. Much larger than the similarly colored Dusky Honeyeater.

name: Little Green-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern thailand, malay peninsula, and greater sundas
description: This aptly-named forest species is the smallest of the green-pigeons. Males are highly distinctive, with a blue-gray head and neck, orange chest, pinkish-maroon back, and green belly.

name: Rufous-breasted Warbling Finch
rangeDescription: West slope of andes of peru (la libertad to ica)
description: Rare and endangered bird found at high elevations in the western Andes of northern and central Peru. Note the black mask and the reddish-orange eyebrows, throat, and breast.

name: Taiwan Liocichla
rangeDescription: Montane forest of taiwan
description: The gloom of the forest may make this small songbird of dense montane forests and edges appear dark, but a bit of sunlight reveals a gloriously colorful plumage, with subtle patches of olive, blue, yellow, orange, and chestnut. Social, moving about in pairs or flocks, often emerging out into the open when gaps in the vegetation are present.

name: Long-whiskered Owlet
rangeDescription: Cloud forest of northern peru (amazonas and san martín)
description: Tiny owl known only from a small area in the eastern Andes of northern Peru. The long plumes around its eyes and bill are unique among owls.

name: Long-tailed Glossy Starling
rangeDescription: Far southern mauritania to northern guinea eastward to southern sudan and northwestern south sudan
description: A large, extremely long-tailed, dark and glossy starling. Sometimes looks black, but in good light shows iridescence that is mostly blue-green, with a purple belly and tail.

name: Sind Sparrow
rangeDescription: Far southeastern iran to pakistan and northwestern india
description: A small, strikingly patterned sparrow which is extremely similar to the House Sparrow. The male has a bright chestnut eye-stripe, a gray crown and hindneck, a black patch restricted to the chin, a large white shoulder patch, and a black bill.

name: Green Warbler
rangeDescription: Caucasus to northern türkiye, northern iran, and northwestern afghanistan; winters southern india
description: Nondescript leaf warbler with two whitish wing bars (often only one visible), dull to bright greenish upperparts, a yellow wash usually restricted to the face, and a pale orange lower bill. Breeds in forest in the Caucasus mountains.

name: Gray-crowned Tetraka
rangeDescription: Rainforest of eastern madagascar
description: Attractive, medium-sized tetraka. Green back, gray head, white throat, and yellowish underparts.

name: Cocoi Heron
rangeDescription: Widespread south america (excluding the andes)
description: Large and lanky with gray-blue back, white neck, and black cap. Widespread and conspicuous (though not abundant) in marshes, rivers, and lakes from Panama to southernmost Chile and Argentina, usually at low elevations.

name: Townsend's Warbler
rangeDescription: Coniferous forest of western north america; winters to costa rica
description: Brightly-colored warbler with a contrasting face pattern with dark cheeks and crown surrounded by bright yellow. Also shows olive back, bold white wingbars, and yellow on the breast.

name: Glow-throated Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Mountains of western panama (chiriquí and veraguas)
description: Tiny, poorly-known hummingbird with extremely limited range in western Panama. Males are greenish above with rusty flanks, a pinkish-red throat, and a white collar.

name: Indian Yellow-nosed Albatross
rangeDescription: Breeds on southern indian ocean islands; ranges southern oceans
description: Massive seabird, but relatively small and slender for an albatross. Breeds on islands in the Southern Indian ocean from Marion and Prince Edward to Amsterdam and St.

name: Uluguru Mountain Greenbul
rangeDescription: Northeastern tanzania (uluguru mountains)
description: A medium-sized greenbul with a dark cap, an otherwise gray head and underparts, and an olive-green back. Uncommon, inconspicuous, and local in montane forest in the Uluguru Mountains of Tanzania.

name: Guianan Puffbird
rangeDescription: Eastern venezuela, northeastern brazil, and the guianas
description: Chunky, large-billed bird of rainforest canopy; easily identified by black-and-white plumage, relatively large size, and staid demeanor. Most often seen perched high in bare branches, sometimes near arboreal termite nests, in which it digs its own nest cavities.

name: Swinhoe's Rail
rangeDescription: Siberia and northern manchuria; winters to southern china and ryukyu islands (southern japan)
description: This sparrow-sized rail moves like a ghost through grassy meadows and wetlands. Prefers to run instead of fly, but white wing patches are unmistakable if seen.

name: Jamaican Mango
rangeDescription: Jamaica
description: A large dark hummingbird of forest edges, plantations, and gardens. Its black underparts, iridescent red cheeks, and red-purple tail are unique within its range.

name: Yellow-browed Seedeater
rangeDescription: Highlands of southern tanzania to zambia and northern malawi
description: A chunky medium-sized seedeater, brown above and pale below with heavy streaking. Patches of yellow appear on several parts of the body, including the eyebrows, breast, and edges of the wing and tail feathers.

name: Negros Bleeding-heart
rangeDescription: Negros and panay (west visayas; west-central philippines)
description: A very rare medium-sized ground dove of foothill forest floor on Negros and Panay. Iridescent greenish-blue on the head and sides to the chest, scaled on the upper back, with brownish flight feathers.

name: Greater Flamingo
rangeDescription: Southern europe and mediterranean basin to southern africa and indian subcontinent
description: Distributed from Africa and southern Europe through West Asia to South Asia. Very large, with long,

name: Palau Cicadabird
rangeDescription: Palau (western caroline islands)
description: Small cuckooshrike with a restricted range, found only on the Palau Archipelago. Males are mainly gray with a black patch on the face, black tail, and black on the wings.

name: Purple-throated Cotinga
rangeDescription: Tropical southeastern colombia to southeastern peru and western amazonian brazil
description: Striking, ornately-colored cotinga. Male and female are uniquely beautiful: males are black above, white below, with a bright purple throat and breast; females are tawny yellowish with extensive black barring.

name: New Ireland Munia
rangeDescription: New ireland (northeastern bismarck archipelago)
description: A small grassland-loving finch with a light orange chest and belly. Richly brown above, with a black head.

name: White-cheeked Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Montane forest of vietnam and southern laos
description: A garrulous, sociable bird, often found in large flocks, both single-species and mixed. Warm brown with a gray crown, a broad black mask, and a luminously white cheek spot, and long white-tipped tail.

name: Comoro Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Mount karthala on grand comoro island (comoros)
description: Small compact owl with very small ear tufts that are often invisible. Rufous-brown on the underparts and dark brown on the back.

name: Large Elaenia
rangeDescription: Far southeastern colombia to northern argentina and brazil
description: Medium-sized migratory flycatcher found at forest edges, in second growth, and along streams. As with other elaenia species, it has an olive-brown back and yellowish belly.

name: Dusky-throated Hermit
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (southern minas gerais and espírito santo to santa catarina)
description: Small understory hummingbird found in montane forest and dense second growth. Note its strongly curved bill and prominent dark mask and a pale eyebrow.

name: Giant Wood-Rail
rangeDescription: Marshes of southeastern brazil to paraguay, uruguay, and northeastern argentina
description: Easy to recognize by its gigantic size. Note the rusty neck and belly that help to distinguish it from similar smaller wood-rails.

name: Western Shrike-tit
rangeDescription: Southwestern western australia
description: Small bird with short, heavy bill. Green above, with a mainly yellow front except for a broad white belly strip.

name: Pinto's Spinetail
rangeDescription: Northeastern brazil (northeastern maranhão, eastern pernambuco, and adjacent alagoas)
description: Spinetail with a largely dark body contrasting with a rich rusty crown, wings, and tail. Note the streaked whitish throat.

name: White-browed Conebill
rangeDescription: Andes of eastern peru (san martín) and western bolivia
description: Tiny bicolored tanager with a sharp, pointed bill. Orangey red below and bluish gray above, with a strong white eyebrow.

name: Macleay's Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Rainforest of northeastern queensland (cooktown to townsville)
description: Distinctive medium-sized rainforest honeyeater. Underparts are olive with white streaking.

name: Campo Miner
rangeDescription: South-central brazil (minas gerais to são paulo) and adjacent northeastern bolivia
description: Small terrestrial ovenbird with a short tail. Brownish overall, paler below, with a whitish eyebrow and speckled breast.

name: Taiwan Whistling-Thrush
rangeDescription: Mountain streams of taiwan
description: Large songbird, blackish-blue with metallic sheen, appearing black from a distance and in poor lighting. Up close, a brighter blue patch on the shoulder and dark red irides are diagnostic.

name: Peruvian Pigeon
rangeDescription: Northern peru (subtropical marañón valley) and adjacent southern ecuador
description: Large, rusty pigeon confined to the Marañon drainage of northwestern Peru. Its range may extend to extreme southern Ecuador, but evidence is lacking.

name: Gouldian Finch
rangeDescription: Northern australia (kimberley division to western cape york peninsula)
description: A brilliantly colorful, unmistakable bird with vivid green back, yellow belly, purple chest, blue nape, black throat, and very pale bill; face may be red, yellow or black. Juvenile dull olive above, pale below, with paler bill than most other small finch-like birds.

name: West Mexican Chachalaca
rangeDescription: Semiarid western mexico (central jalisco and michoacán to chiapas)
description: Noisy, long-tailed game bird of tropical forest and edge, usually found in small groups. Most often detected by its raucous song, which carries well.

name: Violet-breasted Sunbird
rangeDescription: Savanna of southern somalia and eastern kenya
description: Male is iridescent-green above, with a dark belly and a purple band across the breast. Female is nondescript, with a pale eyebrow and blurry streaking across the pale yellowish underparts.

name: Indian Courser
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed pakistan to india and sri lanka
description: Elegant and stately large plover-like bird. Note typically erect posture, strong black-and-white brow pattern, orange-suffused crown and chest, and slightly downcurved dark bill.

name: Cinnamon Quail-thrush
rangeDescription: Southeastern queensland to northwestern new south wales, central and northeastern south australia, and southeastern northern territory
description: Heavily patterned terrestrial bird of central Australia. Both sexes have pale eyebrow, pale brown back, speckled undertail, and black-and-white markings on wing.

name: Chilean Swallow
rangeDescription: Breeds southern chile and argentina; winters north to bolivia and brazil
description: Common and familiar swallow of southern South America; found widely from the coast to Andean foothills and from open forests to beaches. Often near water and regularly around towns and villages, associating readily with slightly smaller Blue-and-white Swallow.

name: Venezuelan Bristle-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Coastal cordillera of northern venezuela (carabobo to distrito federal)
description: Small olive-yellow flycatcher with black ear patch, gray crown, pinkish lower mandible, and bold, contrasting yellowish wing bars. Sexes similar.
